content.introduction: Under the Trump administration, the stock market saw significant growth driven by corporate earnings, tax cuts, and favorable Federal Reserve policies. Key tech stocks were actively traded by President Trump himself. The market's resilience was attributed to strong economic fundamentals despite external risks.
body: [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.usbank.com/content/usbank/us/en/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html&title=Stocks+Under+the+Trump+Administration%3A+What+is+Driving+Markets+in+2026%3F+%7C+U.S.+Bank&summary=See+how+tariffs%2C+tax+cuts%2C+oil+prices%2C+and+earnings+are+shaping+the+stock+market+under+Trump+in+2026+and+what+investors+should+watch+next.&media=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.usbank.com%2Fcontent%2Fdam%2Fusbank%2Fen%2Fimages%2Fphotos%2Fwealth-management%2Fphoto-white-house-exterior-close-16x9.jpg). Since the 2024 presidential election, the S&P 500’s total return climbed more than 25% as of April 20, 2026, despite meaningful volatility along the way.[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_3281) “Investors have overcome concerns about geopolitical conflict and trade announcements and focused on fundamental strength, namely corporate earnings growth,” says Bill Merz, head of capital markets research for U.S. Bank Asset Management Group. S&P 500 companies increased fourth-quarter 2025 revenue by 9.2% and earnings by 13.4%, while first-quarter results are exceeding analyst expectations of 9.6% revenue growth and 13.0% earnings growth.[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_77a2) Those fundamentals help explain why investors have continued to buy stocks despite higher oil prices, tariff uncertainty and persistent geopolitical risk. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act ([OBBBA](https://www.usbank.com/wealth-management/financial-perspectives/financial-planning/the-real-impact-of-the-tax-cuts-and-jobs-act.html)) lowered corporate and individual taxes, and federal tax refunds were running approximately $47 billion higher than in 2025 through April 24.[4](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_e463) Earlier Federal Reserve rate cuts also helped support borrowing and spending, giving investors another reason to maintain a constructive market view.

President [Donald Trump](https://www.cnbc.com/donald-trump/) reported thousands of financial transactions totaling hundreds of millions of dollars — including large purchases and sales of tech giants [Nvidia](/quotes/NVDA/), [Microsoft](/quotes/MSFT/), [Amazon](/quotes/AMZN/) and [Meta](/quotes/META/) — in the first three months of 2026, new [disclosure forms](https://www.oge.gov/web/OGE.nsf/Officials%20Individual%20Disclosures%20Search%20Collection?OpenForm) reveal. The transactions, which became public on Thursday, are valued at between $220 million and $750 million cumulatively, according to [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/trump-ethics-filing-reveals-thousands-trades-tied-us-corporate-securities-2026-05-14/). The timing of some of the president's transactions overlapped with news from the companies whose stock he was buying or selling, the news outlet [NOTUS](https://www.notus.org/money/donald-trump-stock-investments-palantir-axom-nvidia) reported Thursday. One week after Trump's Feb. 10 purchase of between $1 million and $5 million of Nvidia stock, for instance, that company [announced](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/17/meta-nvidia-deal-ai-data-center-chips.html) a major chip deal with Meta. The president also bought between $500,000 and $1 million worth of Nvidia stock one week before the Commerce Department officially [approved](https://www.bis.gov/press-release/department-commerce-revises-license-review-policy-semiconductors-exported-china?utm_source=chatgpt.com) the sale of some Nvidia chips to China, NOTUS reported.
